contracts.detail: Two distinct TIM1/TIM8 16-bit counters, each with 16-bit repetition, seven compare channels, capture and external main/complementary outputs only1..4. Channels5..7 internal compare/status only, no corresponding CC interrupt enable or DMA request. Shared timebase/control/output resources inside each timer require ownership. No family-only TIM3/4/5/16/17 or ADC2/3 producer admission.

Timer kernel fixed HCLK; APB2 gate controls register access, requiring two bus clocks after enabling. Sleep operation subject to LPEN; Stop stops timer with retained registers/no wake IRQ; Standby loses state. Debug freeze is only when core halted with respective DBG_TIM_STOP; freezes counter and disables outputs, delayed-break behavior can apply. Software Init/DeInit is not peripheral reset.

PSC always buffered; ARPE controls ARR preload, OCxPE compare preload; RCR loads at UEV and schedules updates everyREP+1 overflow/underflow events. Center-aligned uses half-period events and initial write/start ordering changes odd-REP phase. UG initializes counter/PSC/repetition and can affect TRGO, even if URS suppresses request; UDIS suppresses preload update but not counter/prescaler reset. ARR0 blocks counting; UIF/UIOVRF are pending history, not a queue.

DIR cannot be written in center/encoder modes; edge-to-center transition requires CEN0, DIR and CMS must not change simultaneously. Avoid writing CNT while running center mode. DITHEN requires CEN0; disabling additionally requiresARPE0 then clearingCCIF before restart and restoring compatible period/compare encoding. Fractional patterns span16edge periods or8center periods; max0xFFFEF, CNT integer only, capture values shifted4.

CCxS only writable with CCxE0; selector3TRC requires internalTS. Paired paths1/2,3/4 and TISEL/XOR/filter resources are shared. CaptureCCRread clearsCCIF, CCxOF requireswrite0; read data before overcapture flag to avoid missing newly arrived overcapture. DMA and IRQ/CPU reads share that history. CC prescaler resets whenCCxE0. CCPC can preload capture polarity too; register write need not immediately change active polarity.

Gated mode forbidsTI1edge-detector. Triggers may startCEN independently of HAL state; StopCEN alone leaves slave armed. Encoder requiresNP0, appropriate input mappings/polarity and ARR. Break configuration setters check software IDLE and parameters but do not establish the complete CEN/MOE/LOCK/readback protocol. BREAK_EnableInput, DisableInput and RearmInput explicitly permit IDLE or ACTIVE. Enabling break2 does not establish OSSI=OSSR=1 or the required exclusion with delayed break. RearmInput sets disarm and polls clear without establishing MOE=0, waiting for all system conditions or clearing SBIF; timeout leaves the request set. Callback completion is not fault-recovery permission.

SetDeadtimewritesBDTRthenDTR2; SetLockLevelseparateBDTRRMWcanfollowpriorBDTRwritewhichalreadyfrozeLOCKperRM. HALdoesnotverifyacceptance. BreakDelaysetterpermitsACTIVEandwritesall8bitsincludingnonpreloadedscale; modeconfigonlysoftwareIDLEnotCEN0. Overridealso requiresactualMOE0andunlockedstates beyondsoftwarechannelstate.

General and split IRQ handlers read SR and DIER once. Each enabled CCxIF is cleared before dispatching the capture/compare callback; the HAL handler does not read CCR and does not check or clear CCxOF. If a capture arrives after the clear but before the caller reads CCR, the CCR read can consume the newly set CCxIF and return the newer capture, with no second callback for that event. The caller owns capture values and overcapture detection/write-0 clearing. Later callbacks use the earlier flag/enable snapshot even if an earlier callback changes configuration. Update handlers clear UIF but leave UIOVRF history. Active break conditions may keep or reassert flags. Do not infer quiescence or event counts from callbacks.

Global Stop_DMA removes remembered burst request from enabled UDE/COMDE/TDE before selecting one DMA handle. Request-to-index defaults UPD for zero or unmatched combinations. If remembered burst source equals only enabled global request, subtraction produces zero and abort still targets UPD while excluded request stays enabled. Remembered configuration is insufficient ownership bookkeeping; forbid overlap/stale source before relying on this stop path. No observed occurrence claimed. Unlike channel stop, global Stop_DMA disables the selected request mask before abort, then clears CEN and sets IDLE. A multi-bit mask such as UDE|TDE (with no burst exclusion) disables both requests but falls through the exact-match index switch to UPD, aborting only that DMA handle; the other transfer is not independently aborted. Fallback UPD may be unlinked: Init does not initialize hdma slots, and TIM_Abort_DMA only debug-asserts non-NULL. With assertions off a zero-initialized unlinked slot can be dereferenced while installing the abort callback on the non-silent path; uninitialized storage instead makes the pointer indeterminate. Do not assume a specific fault/outcome or infer quiescence; initialize and link every handle actually selected.

SetConfigDMABurst allows global IDLE or ACTIVE and updates shared DCR plus remembered source without stopping prior transfer. StartDMABurst only assertion-validates source; unconfigured NONE=0 can yield index underflow when assertions disabled. It enables request before DMA start and leaves it on failure; it does not start CEN or set independent burst-active state. Stop uses current remembered source, ignores Abort_IT result, disables request after abort, and leaves source remembered. Explicit admission, source immutability and completion ownership required. StartDMABurst installs TIM_DMAStopCallback for abort for every source, including CC channels; accepted abort completion therefore reports global stop rather than channel-stop identity. StopDMABurst discards Abort_IT failure and does not synthesize a callback itself (unlike TIM_Abort_DMA); it does not guarantee any completion callback. DeInit retains dmaburst_source and DCR; Init resets only the remembered source, leaving hardware DCR until explicitly configured/reset.

A DMA read of CCR has the same capture-flag clearing side effect as a CPU read. Concurrent CC interrupt service and DMA consumption therefore share capture/overcapture history; independent lossless per-event callbacks cannot be assumed. CCDS=1 requests capture DMA on update rather than a new capture, so repeated or old CCR data can be read and the flag consumed by an update-driven transfer. Own capture production, CCR consumption and event accounting together.

DeInit clears CEN, writes DIER=0 and SR=0, then attempts blocking abort for enabled DMA request handles and ignores abort returns. Writing SR=0 discards clearable event history including overcapture/UIOVRF; active level-sensitive BIF/B2IF/SBIF need not clear. It clears channel enables through LL and publishes RESET, but CCPC can defer complementary-channel enable changes until COM. It leaves MOE/AOE, SMS/TS, MMS/MMS2, BDTR and DCR unchanged; a later slave trigger can set CEN again. Reset software states and HAL return do not establish stopped hardware, drained DMA or safe pin levels.
